notes: HXEXT as a LINKed program: the COMMAREA sibling of cruc-hx-extended-cursor, which is a terminal transaction (HX02). The det port's LINK-entry code (the DFHCOMMAREA copy-in, the COMMAREA hand-back caBack) is reached only by a LINK entry (#7955: the caBack survivors of cruc-hx-extended-cursor, `det_mutation.py sibling`). Scenarios are inputs of the base case entered by LINK with STARTCODE D (IBM: a task started for a distributed program link, X19). Run through the det port (`det_port.py run cruc-hx-extended-linked --work DIR`), never plain `equivalence.py run`, whose forge stub does not port the LINK body (#6166). Same source as cruc-hx-extended-cursor; LICENSE and NOTICE are the cics-crucible's own.

scenarios.name: link-good-entry
scenarios.why: a valid account: the OK message is STRINGed, SEND MAP DATAONLY without CURSOR

scenarios.name: link-pf5-blink
scenarios.why: PF5: BLINK-MISTAKE, X'F1' in the attribute byte next to DFHBLINK in the highlight byte

scenarios.name: link-bad-account
scenarios.why: CHECK-INPUT: ACCTL is not 6: the field is re-sent red, blinking, cursor by -1 in its length

scenarios.name: link-tail-enter
scenarios.why: #7955: a LINK whose COMMAREA (8 bytes, EIBCALEN 8) is longer than HXEXT's DFHCOMMAREA storage: the bytes past it are kept (Storage.beyond) and go back to the caller, each distinct; the area each side left is compared whole (caller_bytes_diff, #7954 X10)
